s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of skin lesions with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory results
salient_findings: Numerous irregular, erythematous papules and nodules on the abdomen and lower back
Leukopenia, anemia, mild thrombocytopenia, and neutropenia
Elevated C-reactive protein and alkaline phosphatase
key_facts: Skin lesions on abdomen and lower back
Denies weight loss, chills, abdominal pain, bleeding, or healing problems
Numerous moderately severe, irregular, erythematous papules and nodules on examination
Negative panel for sexually transmitted infections
Shave biopsy showed dense infiltrate of monotonous neoplastic cells

differentials: Primary cutaneous aggressive epidermotropic CD8+ T-cell lymphoma
per_call: Primary cutaneous aggressive epidermotropic CD8+ T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory results, consistent with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Leukemia cutis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia, suggesting leukemia cutis

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with erythematous papules and nodules, consistent with mycosis fungoides

shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory results, consistent with Sézary syndrome

shortlist.label: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with dense infiltrate of monotonous neoplastic cells, consistent with blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm

raw.rationale: The presence of a dense infiltrate of monotonous neoplastic cells with dispersed chromatin and a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio in the dermis, along with systemic symptoms such as leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia, is more consistent with Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm, a rare and aggressive hematologic malignancy that often presents with skin lesions and bone marrow involvement.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While it can present with skin lesions, the biopsy findings and systemic symptoms do not specifically align with the typical presentation of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Leukemia cutis
rejected.why: Leukemia cutis refers to the infiltration of the skin by leukemic cells, but the specific findings in this case, including the type of cells seen on biopsy, do not directly point to a known leukemia as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: Mycosis fungoides is the most common form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and typically has a more indolent course, with different biopsy findings that usually show epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes.

rejected.label: Sézary syndrome
rejected.why: Sézary syndrome is an aggressive form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma characterized by erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, and the presence of Sézary cells in the blood, which does not match the specific presentation and biopsy findings in this case.
